subject: Culture
title: Sky Burial
description: A quick, practical guide to Sky Burial.

hook.text: In Tibet, the dead are carried to mountaintops and offered to vultures. It's called sky burial.

buildup.text: Tibetan Buddhists believe the soul has already left. The body is just an empty vessel to return to nature.

discovery.text: A rogyapa—body breaker—prepares the remains so vultures can consume them completely.

twist.text: China banned sky burials during the Cultural Revolution. The ban was lifted in the 1980s after Tibetan protests.

climax.text: Sky burial treats the body as a final act of generosity. Even in death, you give.

punchline.text: The last gift is the body itself.

quiz.question: In Tibetan Buddhism, why is the body given to vultures?
options: The soul has left and the body is returned to nature

details.summary: Tibetan sky burial offers the body to vultures on a high mountaintop after death. A rogyapa prepares the body while monks chant prayers. The practice embodies Buddhism's teaching on impermanence — the body is an empty vessel, and its final act should be generously feeding other living beings.
details.whyItMatters: Sky burial transforms death from loss into generosity. It challenges the universal assumption that bodies deserve preservation, offering instead the radical compassion of giving one's flesh to sustain other life.
takeaways: Sky burial reflects Buddhist teachings about bodily impermanence
The body is offered as a final act of compassion to feed vultures
A rogyapa specialist prepares and presents the body

faq.question: Why choose sky burial over other funeral methods?
faq.answer: Practical and spiritual reasons converge. Tibet's rocky, frozen ground makes grave-digging difficult. Wood for cremation is scarce at high altitude. Spiritually, Buddhists believe the body after death is an empty vessel — keeping it intact serves no purpose.

faq.question: What role does the rogyapa play?
faq.answer: The rogyapa (body-breaker) is a specialized practitioner who prepares the body for consumption. They may cut the body, crush bones, and mix remains with barley flour and yak butter to attract vultures.
